display.title: A Trip to Another World: Every Jew's Share in Olam Haba
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi takes children on a journey further than outer space, to Olam Haba, and explains Kol Yisroel, the fourth of the Twelve Pesukim.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi invites children on a trip further than outer space, to another world. The Torah teaches that there are two worlds: Olam Hazeh, the world we live in now, and Olam Haba, the world to come, where the soul goes after a person's life here. Our Sages say that even 120 years of the best pleasures in this world cannot equal one second of the soul's joy in Olam Haba, which Hashem reserved as a reward for the Torah we learn and the mitzvos we do. Every child has a share waiting there, and the more Torah and mitzvos, the greater the pleasure. Uncle Yossi quotes the Gemara in Sanhedrin: all of Yisroel have a share in the world to come, for 'your people are all tzaddikim'. This is Kol Yisroel, number four of the Twelve Pesukim, and the clip ends as the march to its tune is about to begin.
display.lesson: Every Jew has a special place waiting in Olam Haba, and each bit of Torah and each mitzvah adds to its joy.
